**STEP 1 - Scene:** This isn't an overhead photo of a plated meal. It's a side view of a single whole Royal Gala apple (sticker PLU 4174, Chile) sitting directly on a dark tablecloth. The plate of toast at the edge isn't part of this item.

**STEP 2 - Vessel:** There's no vessel. The apple sits on the table, so I estimated its size directly. Judging by the PLU sticker (~2.5 cm across), the apple is about 7.5–8 cm in diameter.

**STEP 3 - Items:** One whole raw Gala apple with skin. There's no sauce or oil.

**STEP 4 - Area:** Plate coverage doesn't apply. I treated the apple as a slightly flattened sphere about 7.8 cm wide and 7 cm tall.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** Volume ≈ 4/3 × π × 3.9 × 3.9 × 3.5 ≈ 223 ml (outer envelope).

**STEP 6 - Grams:** A whole apple is solid flesh with a small core cavity, so its density is about 0.8–0.85 g/ml. That gives about 223 × 0.82 ≈ 183 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** A raw apple has about 52 kcal per 100 g, so 183 g × 0.52 ≈ 95 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** A medium-large Gala apple typically weighs 150–200 g and has 80–105 kcal, so this estimate is plausible.
